# Glossary

The research notes in `docs/research/` were written while the work happened and
use the project's working vocabulary freely. This page defines the terms a new
reader meets most often. Where a term has its own document, that document is
named.

## Measurement and method

**Ground truth.** An audio export made by ReBirth itself from a song. Every
behavioural claim in this project rests on comparing such an export with
Reborn's render of the same song. No ReBirth export is in the repository.

**Fixture.** A small song generated by `tools/rbsgen/` to exercise one control
of one device, with everything else silent and the effects off. A fixture set
sweeps a control across its range, at least three points and preferably five.
Fixtures are made by our own code and are not ReBirth's songs, but the sets
used for the research were kept in the author's workspace and are not
published; `examples/` holds four songs made the same way.

**Batch (batchH, batchI and so on).** One dated round of fixtures and exports,
named by a letter. The notes cite a batch to say which measurements a claim
rests on.

**Cell.** One fixture in a sweep, scored as a single comparison. "30 of its 40
cells moved" means a change altered the score of 30 fixtures in a 40-fixture
batch.

**Isolation.** The rule that a comparison sounds one device, one instance of
it, and one effect or none, proved by rendering rather than assumed.
`tools/rbsgen/isolation_check.py` tests a fixture before it is exported.
`docs/MEASUREMENT_PROTOCOL.md` has the full rule.

**Null pair.** The same fixture rendered by both programs with no effects,
played first in every listening batch so the listener knows how close the two
are before anything else changes.

**Ear check.** A short listening comparison of our render against ReBirth's
export, used alongside measurement and never in place of it.

**Hold-out.** Fixtures kept out of a fit and used only afterwards, to show that
a fitted law predicts settings it was not tuned on.

**Parity.** Agreement with ReBirth's measured behaviour, the project's goal for
every device. "Parity work" means work toward it. In the mod reader the same
word has an unrelated meaning, see *Key parity* below.

**Supertask.** One component (the 303, the 808, the 909, the PCF, the delay,
the compressor or the distortion) taken to parity on its own, with nothing else
changed while it was open. A finding about another component was written into
`docs/BACKLOG.md` instead of fixed. `docs/research/METHOD.md` describes it.

**Worklist.** The live document of a supertask, for example
`docs/research/PLAN_303_ENVELOPE.md`, where its open laws and next measurements
were kept.

**Role A and Role B, the two-role wall.** The procedure used for the effects
from September 2026. Role A measured ReBirth and wrote a behavioural
specification (`docs/specs/`); Role B, a separate context that saw only the
specification, the measured data and the codebase, wrote and fitted the
implementation. `docs/PROVENANCE.md` explains why.

**Byte-neutral check.** `tools/render/byte_neutral.py` renders the demo songs
that ship with your own copy of ReBirth before and after a change and compares
the output bytes, which proves a change meant to alter no sound altered none on
the paths those songs take.

**Platform baseline.** `tools/measure/platform_baseline.py` and
`docs/baselines/`: measurements of a fixed set of fixtures recorded on the
reference Windows machine, which CI and a new machine are checked against
within a stated tolerance. Bit-identical output across compilers is not
expected; agreeing measurements are.

**`regress_ab`.** `tools/analyze/regress_ab.py`, which scores a change across
every fixture set at once by spectral shape, so a fit tuned on one batch cannot
quietly worsen the others.

## The song file

**Chunk and track.** A `.rbs` file holds each device's settings twice. The
chunk is the panel as it looked when the song was saved; the track is the
automation that plays. Song mode plays the track. `docs/FORMAT_RBS.md`.

**Tick and the tick-0 dump.** A track's events are timed in ticks, 32 to a
bar. A song states its starting settings as a burst of events at tick 0, and
that dump, not the chunk, is what a render starts from.

**Song mode and pattern mode.** ReBirth's two transport modes: song mode plays
the recorded arrangement and its automation, pattern mode loops the selected
patterns with the panel as set.

**Accent row.** Column 0 of a drum pattern, which carries the accent. It holds
a value, not a flag: the 808 writes 1 and the 909 writes 2.

**Shared column.** One of the 808's five pattern columns that holds two
instruments (low tom and low conga, for example), switched by a byte in the
808 chunk.

## Devices and sound

**TPT voice.** Reborn's own 303, built on topology-preserving-transform
filters and fitted to ReBirth by measurement. It is the default voice and the
only one the parity work targeted.

**Open303.** Robin Schmidt's MIT-licensed 303 emulation, vendored in
`third_party/open303` and selectable per slot. It models the hardware rather
than ReBirth and was never tuned toward ReBirth. Measurements never use it.

**Chirp.** The audible sweep of the 303 filter's resonant peak as its
envelope moves, the part of the 303's character that took longest to work on;
on retriggered mid-resonance notes it is still a little muted, an accepted
residual.

**PCF.** The pattern-controlled filter, ReBirth's step-triggered filter effect,
with 55 trigger patterns.

**Sample path and synthesis path.** The 808 and 909 play either loaded samples
or Reborn's own synthesis. Each path has its own **trim table** of per-voice
level corrections, chosen by whether a sample is loaded.

## Mods

**Mod.** A `.rbm` archive that replaces ReBirth's samples and artwork, made with
ReBirth's ModPacker utility. No mod is in the repository. `docs/FORMAT_RBM.md`.

**Partial mod.** A mod that replaces only some of the drum sounds.

**Generated keys.** The scrambling keys the reader computes exactly from two
sums over the readable part of an archive.

**Key parity.** A mod entry's even or odd half; each half is scrambled with its
own key, and each key is confirmed separately.

**Self-check.** The test that decides whether a set of keys decodes an archive
correctly: clean JPEG scans, sample levels and residuals, no wrapped samples.

**Wrap test, unrelated keys and near misses.** The ways a key is confirmed
before it is trusted: a long run of samples that wrong keys would wrap, audio
too far from uniform for an unrelated key to pass by chance, and a check that
no neighbouring sum's key decodes the archive better.

**Estimator.** The fallback that recovers keys from an archive's content when
the generated keys do not fit, taking a few seconds.
